name: Moonlight / Sunshine
description: The open-source game-streaming pair: Sunshine is the self-hosted server (host), Moonlight is the client. Ultra-low-latency H.264/HEVC/AV1 streaming with hardware encoding, no cloud fees, no subscription.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Sunshine captures via KMS on Wayland (needs one-time setcap); no per-session confirm dialog after that

P2P (Direct Connection).comment: Direct connection to the Sunshine host's IP, over LAN or WAN with port forwarding

Relay Server.comment: No built-in relay/TURN server; WAN access needs port forwarding or a VPN like Tailscale

LAN Discovery.comment: Moonlight auto-discovers Sunshine hosts on the local network via mDNS

Tailscale Support.comment: Works over any reachable network incl. Tailscale, but no native built-in integration

Open Source.comment: Both Sunshine (GPL-3.0) and Moonlight clients are fully open source

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: Streams one selected display at a time, not simultaneous multi-monitor output

Gamepad Passthrough.comment: Flagship feature: virtual Xbox 360/DS4 controller emulation on the host. Not supported on macOS

Microphone Passthrough.comment: No client-mic-to-host passthrough; the macOS mic permission is only for host audio capture

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Moonlight client adjusts to network conditions; Sunshine exposes bitrate/FEC tuning

AV1 Codec.comment: AV1 Main 8-bit/10-bit, on GPUs with AV1 encode support

Session Sharing.comment: One active Moonlight client per Sunshine instance at a time

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Streams the host's single active display/session, not isolated multi-user terminal sessions

Virtual Display.comment: Sunshine can create/manage a virtual display for headless streaming (Windows)

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: Video-codec based streaming (H.264/HEVC/AV1), standard chroma subsampling, not full 4:4:4

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: Sunshine can stream at very high frame rates; actual FPS depends on host GPU encoder and network

ISO Mounting.comment: Not a VM/KVM tool; game-streaming only

Wake-on-LAN.comment: Moonlight can send a WoL packet to wake the Sunshine host before connecting

Pre-Login Access.comment: Sunshine must be running as a logged-in session/service; no pre-login BIOS-style access

No Account Required.comment: One-time PIN pairing between Moonlight and Sunshine; no cloud account needed

2FA / MFA.comment: Just one-time PIN pairing plus a web UI username/password; no ongoing 2FA

Address Book.comment: Moonlight keeps a simple list of paired hosts, not a full team address book

RBAC.comment: Single admin credential set for the Sunshine web UI; no role-based permissions

Generic USB Passthrough.comment: Only emulated game controllers are passed through, not arbitrary USB devices

UAC Handling.comment: Depends on the capture backend used; not clearly documented across all methods

HDR Support.comment: HEVC Main10/AV1 10-bit HDR streaming on supported GPUs (Windows and Linux via VAAPI)

OTA Updates.comment: Updated manually via installer/package manager; no built-in auto-update push

Windows: Host.comment: Sunshine's most mature and widely-used platform

macOS: Host.comment: Sunshine via VideoToolbox/CoreGraphics; gamepad passthrough not supported on macOS

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Via the KMS capture backend, requires a one-time setcap on the binary

Linux: Client.comment: Moonlight for Linux, also used on Steam Deck and Raspberry Pi builds

Android: Host.comment: Sunshine does not run as a host on Android

Android: Client.comment: One of the most popular Moonlight clients, incl. NVIDIA Shield

Web Browser: Client.comment: No official browser-based Moonlight client; only community/experimental projects exist

NVIDIA RTX 4090.comment: No official published benchmark table; performance follows NVENC encoder tier

Apple Silicon GPU (Metal).comment: Uses Apple VideoToolbox for hardware encoding on macOS hosts

Free Tier.comment: Completely free and open source, no paid tiers at all
